How it works

MB Survey records every Wi-Fi network your phone can see while you walk, and ties each reading to the position you mark on the floor plan. From these readings it builds heatmaps and the report, and exports files for Ekahau and other tools.

Before you start

1. Grant location, nearby Wi-Fi devices and notification permissions (Android requires them to read networks).
2. Turn on location.
3. Disable Wi-Fi scan throttling: Settings → About phone → tap "Build number" 7 times → Developer options → "Wi-Fi scan throttling" OFF. Otherwise Android allows only 4 scans every 2 minutes and the survey is useless. A red banner shows while it is on.

1. Project

Create a project (customer, site, surveyor) or use Import .esx to load an existing Ekahau project: floor plans, scale and planned access points are imported so you can validate the design on site.

2. Floor plan

Add floor → Draw floor plan to draw it on the phone: set the size in metres, add rooms and areas (with names), walls and racking, tap an edge to add a door. The scale is calibrated automatically. Or load an image (JPG/PNG) or a PDF; a photo of a sketch works too. One floor per level.

3. Calibration

Open the floor, choose Calibrate, tap two points at a known distance (a wall, a bay between columns, a door) and enter the metres. Needed for m² areas, heatmap radius and the Ekahau scale. The longer the reference distance, the better.

4. Survey

In Survey mode press the red button, name it and choose:
• Continuous: tap exactly where you stand, walk in a straight line at a steady pace, tap the point you reached when you turn or stop, and so on. Scans taken along the leg are spread by time: do not stop mid-leg and do not change direction without tapping.
• Stop-and-go: tap the point, stand still until the app collects the configured scans, move and tap the next point. Slower but more accurate: good for narrow aisles.
The bottom box shows scans taken and networks seen: it must grow every 2–3 seconds. Undo removes the last point. Press the button again to finish: the survey is saved in the project. In a warehouse walk every aisle, both ways if the racks are tall.

4b. Camera survey (AR)

In the start dialog choose Camera survey: you see the environment through the camera, the mini map top-right with your position and the signal bars at the bottom. First tap: mark on the map where you are. Heading: look down an aisle and tap a map point in front of you, aligning the compass with the floor plan. Then walk: step detector and compass move the dot; when you stop for 2 seconds the app asks whether to record the point. If the dot drifts, tap the mini map and correct it. Points and scans are identical to a classic survey.

5. Heatmaps

Use the three menus at the top to choose metric, SSID and band. Metrics: primary signal (strongest AP), secondary (roaming redundancy), estimated SNR, number of APs above threshold, channel interference, latency and packet loss (active survey), single BSSID. Menu ⋮ → Legend for scales, min/avg/max, surveyed area and coverage percentages. Thresholds are in Settings.

6. Access points

Update APs from measurements creates one AP per group of detected BSSIDs, placed by the strongest samples. In AP mode tap the map where an AP really is. In the AP card rename it, add vendor/model and mark yours (the others are neighbouring networks).

7. Export

Project menu → Export:
• PDF report: summary, heatmaps per floor with statistics, notes, AP and BSSID tables.
• CSV: one row per reading (time, position in px and metres, BSSID, SSID, dBm, channel, latency), for Excel or other tools.
• Ekahau .esx: project openable in Ekahau AI Pro (File → Open Project) with floor plans, scale, placed APs and detected radios: the base to continue the design on the PC. The with surveys variant adds paths and readings in a format Ekahau does not document: try it, and fall back to the standard one if it does not open. All measurements are inside the archive anyway (mbsurvey-measurements.json) and in the CSV.
• PNG: heatmaps as images.
• Backup .zip: full project, importable on another phone.
Every file can be shared (mail, Drive, Teams) or saved on the phone.

Active survey

In Settings → Active survey the app pings the gateway (or a host of your choice) after every scan and records latency and packet loss per point. Two more heatmaps and two report pages appear. You must be connected to the customer\'s network.

Network tools

From the wrench icon: connection status (SSID, BSSID, channel, link rate, IP, gateway, DNS, public IP), ping with jitter, traceroute, subnet scan with MAC and vendor (for another VLAN enter its subnet: it must be reachable through the gateway), port scan, DNS, HTTP speed test (best with a LAN server), channel chart and the full list of Wi-Fi networks with AP vendor. Every result can be shared as text.

Tips

Hold the phone in front of you at the height of the devices the customer will use. Walk at about 1 m/s. Do not cover the phone with your hand. To compare two surveys in the same project filter by SSID or use "Compare two surveys". Smartphone readings differ by a few dB from a professional adapter: use them for validation and troubleshooting, not for certified acceptance tests.
